history.dynasty: Pallava origins per local accounts; 10th-century renovation reported; later Vijayanagara-era additions
history.period: Ancient (Swayambhu deity); structural history from c. 9th-10th century with later renovations
history.summary: CSV town correction: the temple is not in Nellore city but at Penchalakona village in Rapur mandal, Nellore district, about 80 km west of Nellore at the foothills of the Veligonda range. Dedicated to Lord Lakshmi Narasimha, counted among the Nava Narasimha kshetras. Legend says that after slaying Hiranyakashipu, Narasimha's fury would not subside, so Lakshmi appeared as the tribal woman Chenchu Lakshmi and embraced (in Telugu, 'penu vesukonuta') him here — giving the place the name Penusila, later Penchalakona. The deity is regarded as Swayambhu, self-manifested as a huge rock in Yoga mudra; it is also called Somasila Narasimha and Chatravati Narasimha (sages held umbrellas over the Lord at nearby Bhairavakona, and devotees still offer silver and gold umbrellas). One source dates the temple's construction to the 9th century under the Pallavas and another reports a 10th-century renovation — treat both as tradition rather than established fact. The Kandaleru river (once Kanva Nadi, after sage Kanva) flows behind the temple, and a seasonal waterfall nearby adds to its setting.

name: Sri Penusila Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple
town_description: Penchalakona is a village in Rapur mandal of Nellore district, about 80 km west of Nellore, set at the foothills of the Veligonda range. It is an ancient pilgrim centre whose identity is inseparable from the Lakshmi Narasimha temple; the Kandaleru river rises in the surrounding hills and a seasonal waterfall draws visitors in the monsoon months.

travel.railway: Gudur Junction, approx. 63 km; Nellore station is approx. 80 km.
travel.road: Approx. 80 km by road from Nellore; government and private buses run from across Andhra Pradesh; the temple trust provides choultries for pilgrims.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; the annual Brahmotsavams at Narasimha Jayanti in Vaisakha (April-May) are the grandest time to visit.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Approx. 6:30 AM to 12:30 PM and 3:00 PM to 7:30 PM (verify — sources disagree: one listings site shows 8:00 AM to 7:00 PM weekdays). Extended hours on festival days and weekends; no entry fee, special sevas (e.g. Kalyanotsavam) ticketed.
